preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the setMaxWalletAmount function with a very large denominator (e.g., type(uint256).max) to set maxWalletAmount to zero, effectively preventing any non-excluded wallet from holding tokens. This violates the intended functionality of the max wallet limit.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an owner-only function setMaxWalletAmount(uint256 _maxWalletAmountPct) that sets maxWalletAmount = _tTotal / _maxWalletAmountPct. By passing a denominator larger than _tTotal (like type(uint256).max), the division results in zero due to integer rounding. This violates the intended max wallet limit functionality by preventing any non-excluded wallet from holding tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setMaxWalletAmount with type(uint256).max to force maxWalletAmount to zero.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address from the contract. 2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 3. Call setMaxWalletAmount(type(uint256).max). 4. Verify that maxWalletAmount is now zero.
